messages:
liz_support: FYI — Customer CometAnalytics opened a ticket: seeing intermittent 5xx on hosted inference POST /v1/generate since ~08:10 PST. ~15% of requests return 502/504. Sample request-ids: req_7a1b2c, req_7a1b9f. No config changes from them. Can we triage?

jake_oncall: I'm taking. Which region/cluster? Any deploys in last hour? :eyes:

liz_support: They're on prod-us-west1, model redwood-l2, route policy = customer-routed. No deploys recorded in last 2h. Customer traces show control-plane returning 502 for auth/session checks and 504 for routing-policy lookup. Attaching a condensed log snippet below.

liz_support: ```
[08:12:04] controlplane auth-service -> 502 {"req":"req_7a1b2c","err":"session-store timeout"}
[08:12:04] controlplane routing-policy -> 504 {"req":"req_7a1b2c","err":"configdb query timeout"}
[08:12:25] gateway -> 502 {"req":"req_7a1b9f","err":"upstream controlplane 502"}
```

kevin_sre: Seeing the same signal in infra telemetry — config-db query latency spiked and a few session-store calls hit the 10s threshold. Likely DB-side contention + some auth/session cache churn. Correlates with a read-heavy batch job that started ~08:05.

kevin_sre: Short-term mitigation options: (A) bump control-plane config-db timeout to 15s (temporary), (B) enable routing-policy local cache fallback for customer-routed policies, (C) scale controlplane replicas for prod-us-west1. Recommend (B) + (C) first.

maria_prod: I'll spin extra controlplane pods and flip the cache-fallback. Applying a canary patch to prod-us-west1 now.

maria_prod: ```bash
# scale canary controlplane
kubectl -n controlplane scale deployment/controlplane-v2-canary --replicas=4 --context=prod-us-west1
# enable local fallback in configmap (canary)
kubectl -n controlplane patch configmap/routing-config --type merge -p '{"data":{"local_fallback":"true","local_fallback_ttl":"30s"}}'
```

ops_bot: ALERT: controlplane-configdb-timeout spike detected in prod-us-west1 — 23 events/min, p90 latency 11.8s. Pager duty: oncall-jake.

jake_oncall: Thanks. Maria — after canary is healthy, promote to primary. Also adding temporary client-side recommendation to CometAnalytics: exponential backoff + jitter and idempotent retries (max 3). Provide them a header workaround we can honor server-side to bypass policy lookup for urgent traffic.

jake_oncall: Repro steps for infra team to reproduce locally:
1) Send requests to hosted gateway with header `X-Test-Routing=slow`
2) Simulate config-db delay (sleep 12s) on routing-policy query
3) Observe gateway 502/504 responses

jake_oncall: Example curl to reproduce (do not run in prod):
```bash
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -H "X-Debug-Req: repro-1" \
  -H "X-Test-Routing: slow" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-l2","input":"hello"}'
```

liz_support: I emailed the customer with suggested retries and the temporary bypass header approach, plus the support ticket link: https://support.redwood.ai/tickets/CA-4521. They've accepted the mitigation.

kevin_sre: Next actions I've opened: GH #834 "Investigate config-db slow queries during batch jobs" and GH #835 "Add circuit breaker + short-circuit for auth/session calls in controlplane". Quick diagnostic commands below to check DB pool and slow queries:
```bash
# active DB connections (postgres)
psql -c "SELECT count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE datname='configdb';"
# identify slow queries
psql -c "SELECT pid, now()-pg_stat_activity.query_start AS dur, query FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE state='active' ORDER BY dur DESC LIMIT 10;"
```

maria_prod: Canary promoted. Per-metric: gateway 5xx rate dropped from ~15% -> ~2% over last 6m. Rolling restart of a couple older controlplane pods completed. Monitoring 30m. :thumbsup:

jake_oncall: I'll keep the incident in monitoring for 1h and follow up with a short postmortem if the rate doesn't fully clear. Thanks team.

liz_support: Closing loop with customer now. Will keep ticket open until we confirm 0.5% or lower for 1h.

kevin_sre: Logging action items in the incident board. Will check slow-query indexes and consider increasing DB pool quotas.

maria_prod: Noted — will coordinate a maintenance window for the batch job that caused the spike.

ops_bot: INCIDENT NOTE: mitigation applied (routing fallback + scale), alert rate reduced.

jake_oncall: endpoint metrics trending back to normal. Thanks all.
